extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (K-12 school districts, postsecondary institutions, State educational agencies), Title IX Coordinators, school administrators, and legal counsel responsible for Title IX compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Implementing and applying the Department of Education's grievance-procedure requirements under §§106.45 and 106.46 to resolve sex discrimination and sex-based harassment complaints in elementary, secondary, and postsecondary education programs or activities receiving federal funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline standards for §106.45 grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45 sets baseline standards to ensure a fair process under Title IX, including equitable treatment of the parties; decisionmakers who are free of bias or conflicts of interest; adequate notice to the parties of the allegations and timeframes for grievance procedures; guidelines for ensuring the adequate, reliable, and impartial investigation of the complaint; the opportunity for parties to present evidence; and guidelines for how a decisionmaker must assess such evidence and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These baseline standards apply across elementary, secondary, and other recipients and are intended to be minimally prescriptive while ensuring transparent and reliable outcomes; many recipients already have similar protections. The Department anticipates that benefits justify any additional burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures must be in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 106.45(a)(1) and 106.46(a) require that a recipient's grievance procedures be in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must adopt, publish, and implement written grievance procedures to inform the community of Title IX obligations; this requirement dates back to 1975 and is foundational to notice and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and equitable resolution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must provide for the prompt and equitable resolution of sex discrimination complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptness has been required historically and is critical to preventing unnecessary delay; recipients must avoid undue delay while ensuring equity and reliability in outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must implement §106.45 or offer informal resolution under §106.44(k)
rubrics_metrics.description: All recipients must implement grievance procedures consistent with §106.45 or, where available and appropriate, offer informal resolution consistent with §106.44(k) to resolve an allegation of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient may use informal resolution where appropriate, but must ensure any informal process complies with the relevant regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postsecondary institutions' additional obligation (§106.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a recipient that is a postsecondary institution has an additional obligation to implement grievance procedures consistent with §106.46, limited to resolving allegations of sex-based harassment in which either the complainant or respondent is a student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.46 provides additional, student-appropriate protections (e.g., written notice, advisor access, discretion on live hearings) justified by students' age, maturity, and power differentials with employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may use existing processes that do not conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the regulations prohibits a recipient from using an existing process (e.g., procedures in a collective bargaining agreement or other contractual agreement) to satisfy the requirements of §§106.45 and 106.46, so long as those procedures do not conflict with the regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a single existing procedure can avoid undue delay or multiple proceedings; recipients must ensure any adopted existing processes meet all baseline regulatory standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective bargaining agreements must conform to Title IX obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Collective bargaining agreements and other contractual employment arrangements must conform to Federal law as a condition of receiving Federal funds; if a collective bargaining agreement applies to Title IX complaints and does not comply, recipients may need to renegotiate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements are not out of compliance if they adopt options in the final regulations (e.g., live hearing) or set additional procedural requirements that apply equally to the parties. The Department will not require recipients to consult unions but does not prohibit consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal treatment requirement (does not require identical treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must treat parties equally, but equal treatment does not require identical treatment; procedures may recognize distinct rights or protections that apply to employees under collective bargaining agreements or to other parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may adopt additional provisions that apply equally to parties (e.g., timeframes) while still recognizing context-specific rights; see §106.45(j) and discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmakers must be free of bias or conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisionmakers involved in grievance procedures should be impartial and free from bias or conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of baseline standards to ensure fair outcomes; recipients should structure assignments and recusals to avoid biased decisionmakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate notice of allegations and timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must receive adequate notice of the allegations and the timeframes for grievance procedures (including written notice requirements in §106.46(c) for postsecondary settings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written notice supports transparency and allows parties to prepare; recipients must publish and adhere to timeframes, balancing prompt resolution and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for parties to present evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must have the opportunity to present evidence in grievance procedures; §106.46(e)(6) emphasizes an equal opportunity to access relevant evidence that is not otherwise impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should ensure evidence is considered fairly and that parties can meaningfully participate in the fact-finding process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for assessing evidence and credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations require guidance for how a decisionmaker must assess evidence and make credibility determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.46 affords flexibility in assessing credibility in postsecondary sex-based harassment cases (to be responsive to trauma-informed and survivor-centered approaches) while §106.45 provides baseline requirements for other contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements for specified persons (§106.8(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure certain persons receive training related to their duties under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training supports fair and effective implementation of grievance procedures and mitigates power imbalances that may chill reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer and coordination of supportive measures (§106.44(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer and coordinate supportive measures, as appropriate, to support complainants and facilitate reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures help mitigate chilling effects and support complainants in participating in grievance procedures without prejudice to their rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator duties and prompt/effective steps (§106.44(f)(1)(v)/(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator must determine whether to initiate a Title IX grievance procedure and take prompt and effective steps to address sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination duties include assessing whether to proceed with formal grievance procedures even if a party pursues other remedies (e.g., collective bargaining).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion on live hearings and advisor cross-examination (§106.46(f)/(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: In postsecondary sex-based harassment grievance procedures under §106.46, live hearings and cross-examination by a party's advisor are discretionary rather than mandatory; recipients may also permit advisors or experts as allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This discretion aims to create a more survivor-centered and trauma-informed process appropriate to higher education settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallowance or limitation of sensitive or harassing evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.46 permits excluding certain sensitive or harassing evidence from grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should balance relevance with protections against unnecessary retraumatization or harassment in evidence submission and consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules on dismissal and nonparticipating respondents (§106.45(d)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may dismiss complaints when the respondent is not participating in the recipient's education program or activity and is not employed by the recipient, per §106.45(d)(1)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulatory framework clarifies when non-students/non-employees may access grievance procedures and when dismissal is appropriate; factual inquiries determine applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of nondiscrimination policy and grievance procedures (§106.8(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must adopt, publish, and implement a nondiscrimination policy and written grievance procedures consistent with the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication ensures community notice and accountability; recipients may solicit public input but are not required by the Department to hold public hearings prior to adoption except as otherwise required by state/local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX applicability to employees, students, and third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX applies to all sex discrimination occurring under a recipient's education program or activity in the U.S., regardless of whether the person alleged to have engaged in or experienced sex discrimination is a student, employee, or third party participating or attempting to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must apply grievance procedures to complaints involving different identities (employee-to-employee, employee-to-student, student-to-student, non-student participants) consistent with the appropriate section (§106.45 or §106.46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to implement multiple procedures consistent with Title IX
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may maintain different grievance procedures for different categories of complaints (e.g., employee-to-employee, employee-to-student, student-to-student) so long as each set of procedures satisfies §106.45 and, where applicable, §106.46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may choose a single procedure or multiple procedures to address particular legal/contractual obligations, but must ensure compliance with Title IX requirements and avoid conflicting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department technical assistance and coordination with other agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will offer technical assistance as appropriate and coordinates with other Federal agencies (e.g., EEOC) regarding investigations and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients can seek technical assistance to implement regulations; OCR's Case Processing Manual explains investigative/referral boundaries with agencies like the EEOC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory choice not to further define 'employee'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to further clarify the definition of 'employee' in the regulations and expects recipients to determine who qualifies as an employee given local arrangements and state employment law variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the scope of employee reporting obligations and training requirements, recipients should consult the specific discussions of §§106.44 and 106.8(d) and apply reasonable, context-specific judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections apply regardless of employment status (including at-will employees)
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees covered by Title IX should be afforded prompt and equitable grievance procedures when subjected to or alleged to have engaged in sex discrimination; employment status (tenure, part-time, at-will) does not dictate applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department rejects the view that extending these protections to at-will employees exceeds its authority; recipients must ensure procedural protections prior to disciplinary sanctions to prevent discriminatory application of discipline.
